The new offline consumer (crates/scm-sdk/examples/response_compatibility.rs) exercises precisely the reported G25 failures (opaque job-1/p-1/map-1, space-separated and offset-less timestamps, novel enum vocabulary, unknown nested data), the three deliberately retained strict cases, Mode::Request strictness and large-number projection round-trips. No blocker or high finding.

limitations: Read-only review with no shell: I executed nothing. I could not recompute the reviewed source SHA-256 bec9e52c, the archive digests, the retained .local/artifacts crate bytes, or any fingerprint, and I re-ran no cargo, python, node or tsx command. Every pass/fail claim rests on reading the recorded receipts and the code that produces and validates them.

I verified the recorded 56-command list against tools/check_phase.py by reading the composition logic and spot-checking the ordering and de-duplication at each boundary (phase-12 slice [4:25], the phase-19 additions, the two trailing native-export runs). I did not mechanically diff all 56 entries against a computed list, so a single mis-ordered entry in the middle of the list is possible in principle; review_phase.check_evidence would have rejected it at gate time, which is an independent but same-process guard.

Internal consistency of receipts is not authentication. docs/PHASES.md:7 states that repository writers and the invoked reviewer tool are trusted; the hashes detect staleness, not forgery. I could not confirm that the recorded cargo and live executions actually occurred, only that their reports are structurally valid, mutually consistent in source hashes and timestamps, and carry plausible compiler banners, durations and outputs.

Live service acceptance is outside what I can verify. I read docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-14.json as a record; I cannot confirm the requests were made, and the two 400 rejections leave the IAM scope-creation and Gateway provisioning mutation/cleanup chains live-unqualified with an SDK request-shape defect explicitly not excluded.

The registry-and-remote-delivery chunk is pending by declaration. docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json, docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json and any phase-20 remote CI receipt do not exist, so publication, the immutable tag and terminal 49-job CI are unevidenced. I judged this chunk's criteria only and did not penalize those absent later-chunk artifacts.

scripts/check-package.py is deliberately absent from commands_for(20): its --require-clean mode demands an empty working tree including untracked files, so it cannot run inside a gate that writes reports. Package evidence therefore enters this gate indirectly, through check-access-release.py's re-extraction and byte comparison of the retained archives. I consider that sound and it is documented, but it means the archive tests themselves were executed outside the recorded gate run.

I did not re-audit historical phase 1-19 infrastructure, the frozen TypeScript baseline, or prior release receipts beyond what this chunk's artifacts depend on, per the scoping instruction. I read no credential or tenant-registration files and nothing outside this repository.
